findings.claim: On Earth, g is about 10 N/kg. The worked example gives an 80 kg astronaut a weight of 800 N (80 x 10), the flashcard answer says 'About 10 N/kg on Earth' and knowledge check 2 marks '10 N/kg' correct while offering '9.8 m/s' as the only 9.8 option.
findings.truth: AQA works in 9.8 N/kg. The article now reads 9.8 N/kg, the astronaut example recomputes to 784 N, the flashcard matches, and the knowledge check offers 9.8 N/kg with the right unit as the correct option.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.6.1.5 (free fall about 9.8 m/s2) and 4.5.1.3 (the value of g is given in any calculation); recomputation 80 x 9.8 = 784 N

findings.claim: The exam tip tells every student to 'always draw a free body diagram first', a 6-mark practice question requires one, and two flashcards ask for free body diagrams and for resolving forces at an angle by scale drawing.
findings.truth: Free body diagrams and the resolution of forces are Higher tier only. The tip now asks for a labelled force sketch and says free body diagrams are Higher tier; the question and both flashcards carry a (Higher tier) prefix. The article's Resolving Forces box is already wrapped correctly, but its Free Body Diagrams box is not; that wrapper move is left alone because the closing tag is not uniquely addressable.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.1.4: '(HT only) ... use free body diagrams ...' and '(HT only) ... use vector diagrams to illustrate resolution of forces'

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper encloses the whole Elastic Potential Energy section (Ee = 0.5ke^2, its worked example) and the paragraph defining elastic and inelastic deformation.
findings.truth: None of this is Higher tier. Forces and elasticity carries no HT flag, and the elastic potential energy equation sits on the equation sheet with no HT marker, so Foundation students were being told to skip material their paper examines. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3 (no HT flag) and Appendix A given-equations list, equation 6, unmarked

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the key fact that gives v^2 = u^2 + 2as for uniform acceleration.
findings.truth: This equation is given to both tiers on the equation sheet with no HT flag. Foundation students were then asked it untiered in knowledge check 4 and in the 6-mark practice question. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.6.1.5 and Appendix A given-equations list, equation 2, unmarked

findings.claim: The article states flatly that the area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled; practice question 2 asks it, a knowledge check row and two flashcards test it and the tangent method, all untiered.
findings.truth: Both the area under a velocity-time graph and the tangent method on a curved distance-time graph are Higher tier only. The article sentence now says 'At Higher tier'; the practice question, the exam tip and both flashcards carry a Higher tier flag. The match check had one HT-only row among two Foundation rows, so that row was swapped for 'Downward slope / Deceleration', which the same article paragraph already teaches.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.6.1.5 '(HT only) The distance travelled ... can be calculated from the area under a velocity-time graph' and 4.5.6.1.4 '(HT only) ... drawing a tangent'

findings.claim: The required practical box describes only varying the force on a trolley of constant mass.
findings.truth: Required practical 7 has two halves: vary the force at constant mass, and vary the mass at constant force. A sentence for the second half is added.
findings.evidence: spec 8.2.7 / required practical activity 7

findings.claim: The lesson 3 description is 101 characters.
findings.truth: The house validator limit is under 100 characters. Shortened to 77 characters with no loss of meaning.
findings.evidence: house validator limit; measured length 101

findings.claim: A flashcard asks why an object moving in a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity, with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Circular motion at constant speed is Higher tier only. The flashcard now carries a (Higher tier) prefix. The one-clause mention inside the article's velocity paragraph is left alone, since wrapping it would split a both-tier paragraph.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.6.1.3 '(HT only) ... motion in a circle involves constant speed but changing velocity'

findings.claim: Knowledge check 3 and two flashcards ask for inertia with no tier flag, although the article's inertia box is correctly wrapped as Higher tier.
findings.truth: Inertia is Higher tier only. All three now carry a (Higher tier) prefix. The conclusion takeaway still mentions inertia untagged; that is exposure, not assessment, so it is left.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.6.2.1 '(HT only) The tendency of objects to continue in their state of rest or of uniform motion is called inertia'

findings.claim: The momentum and vehicle-safety sections are correctly wrapped as Higher tier in the article, but two practice questions, three knowledge checks, seven flashcards and the exam tip test that material untiered.
findings.truth: The whole momentum topic, including changes in momentum and the safety features that depend on it, is Higher tier only. All twelve items and the exam tip now carry a Higher tier flag. The two conclusion takeaways on momentum stay untagged as exposure.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.7 'Momentum (HT only)', with 4.5.7.3 'Changes in momentum (physics only)' inside it

findings.claim: A key fact states that safety features work by increasing collision time, and the bullet list that follows it ends with ABS brakes.
findings.truth: ABS does not extend the collision time. It stops the wheels locking, so the driver keeps steering control and the braking distance is shorter. The bullet now says so, to stop students writing that ABS increases collision time.
findings.evidence: settled fact; spec 4.5.7.3 lists air bags, seat belts, crash mats, cycle helmets and cushioned surfaces as the rate-of-change-of-momentum examples, and ABS is not among them

findings.claim: Lesson 5 has an empty glossary_terms array although its content carries eight dfn tooltips with definitions.
findings.truth: The in-lesson tooltips still work, but the glossary panel is empty. Not a factual error and not fixable by a surgical text edit; flagged for the glossary backfill pass.
findings.evidence: raw field glossary_terms = []

findings.claim: The required practical is described as using a ripple tank 'to investigate reflection, refraction, and diffraction of water waves'.
findings.truth: Required practical 8 is to identify suitable apparatus and measure the frequency, wavelength and speed of waves in a ripple tank and of waves in a solid. Rewritten to the real method, including the waves-in-a-solid half that was missing.
findings.evidence: spec 8.2.8 / required practical activity 8

findings.claim: A full Diffraction section, a 4-mark practice question, a knowledge check, two flashcards, a glossary term and an exam-tip sentence teach diffraction as examinable.
findings.truth: Diffraction is not in this specification: the string 'diffract' does not occur anywhere in the document. The physics is correct, so the section is kept and labelled as not examined, the exam tip is corrected, and the question, check and two flashcards are prefixed. The glossary term and one conclusion clause are left, since the section label covers them.
findings.evidence: grep of the whole spec for 'diffract' returns no match

findings.claim: The lesson teaches reflection and refraction but names no required practical for them.
findings.truth: Required practical 9 (physics only) is to investigate the reflection of light by different types of surface and the refraction of light by different substances. It is set for this qualification, so a sentence naming it is added to the practical box.
findings.evidence: spec 8.2.9 / required practical activity 9 (physics only)

findings.claim: The key fact explains refraction as a change of speed, and says which way the wave bends when it slows or speeds up; a practice question and two flashcards test the same explanation untiered.
findings.truth: Constructing a ray diagram for refraction is untiered, but explaining refraction by the difference in wave velocity is Higher tier only on this board. The boundary is soft and every Foundation scheme of work teaches it, so this is recorded rather than edited, matching the sibling Combined Science unit.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.2.2: '(HT only) Some effects, for example refraction, are due to the difference in velocity of the waves in different substances'

findings.claim: Common permanent magnets are made from iron, steel, nickel, or cobalt.
findings.truth: Iron is the classic soft magnetic material: it magnetises and demagnetises easily, which is exactly why the same lesson specifies a soft iron core for an electromagnet. Permanent magnets are made from steel and magnetic alloys. Rewritten to separate magnetic materials from permanent-magnet materials.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.1.1 (induced magnetism loses most or all of its magnetism when removed from the field); settled fact

findings.claim: The higher-only wrapper opens at the F = BIl equation, leaving the Motor Effect heading and its definition outside it as untiered content.
findings.truth: The motor effect itself sits inside the HT-only section of the spec, not just its equation. The wrapper now opens above the Motor Effect heading. Electromagnetism, solenoids and electromagnets stay untiered, which is right.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.2.2 'Fleming's left-hand rule (HT only)' opens with 'the magnet ... and the conductor exert a force on each other. This is called the motor effect'

findings.claim: The exam tip tells every student to state F = BIl and use Fleming's left-hand rule; three practice questions, three knowledge checks and six flashcards test the motor effect, F = BIl, Fleming's rule and the d.c. motor untiered.
findings.truth: All of it is Higher tier only. The tip now opens 'At Higher tier' and the twelve assessment items carry a (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.2.2 and 4.7.2.3, both (HT only); Appendix A given-equation 8 HT

findings.claim: This unit is eight lessons built from the Combined Science Paper 2 sequence, so it omits most of the separate-Physics-only content that Paper 2 examines.
findings.truth: Missing, all examinable on this paper: moments, levers and gears (4.5.4, including M = Fd, a recall equation); pressure and pressure differences in fluids (4.5.5, including p = F/A, a recall equation, atmospheric pressure, upthrust and floating, and p = h rho g at Higher tier); sound waves and the 20 Hz to 20 kHz hearing range (4.6.1.4, HT); ultrasound, echo sounding and P- and S-waves (4.6.1.5, HT); lenses, ray diagrams and magnification, and colour and filters (4.6.2.5 onward); perfect black bodies and the temperature of the Earth (4.6.3.2); loudspeakers and microphones (4.7.2.4, 4.7.3.3); induced potential, generators, transformers and the National Grid (4.7.3, HT); the whole of Space physics, topic 8 (4.8); and, smaller, distance versus displacement as the scalar-vector pair (4.5.6.1.1) and radiation dose in sieverts with 1000 mSv = 1 Sv (4.6.2.3). Options: (a) port the sibling science-aqa lessons 9 to 13, which already cover moments, reflection and sound, lenses and colour, induction and transformers, and space physics, and where the same fact-check found their physics sound - but that board's copies were written for Combined Science and the house rule forbids porting between tiers of provision; (b) commission five to six fresh lessons here for the missing topics; (c) leave the gap and label the unit as partial. Recommendation: (b), and treat topic 8 Space physics and the fluids and moments block as the first two builds, since each carries a recall equation or a whole paper topic.
findings.evidence: spec section 2.2 (Paper 2 covers topics 5 to 8) cross-checked against the eight lesson titles in _brief.json

findings.claim: The lesson 1 match check pairs Mass, Weight and Force with 'Kilograms (kg)', 'Newtons (N)' and 'Newtons (N)'.
findings.truth: Two of the three targets are identical, so the Weight and Force rows cannot be distinguished and either ordering is defensible. Both mappings are scientifically right, so no mark is lost; flagged for the question-quality pass rather than rewritten here.
findings.evidence: answer-key inspection

findings.claim: Beyond the limit of proportionality the graph curves and the spring no longer returns to its original length when the force is removed.
findings.truth: The limit of proportionality and the elastic limit are not the same point: a spring can stop obeying Hooke's law and still return to its original length. The spec does not name the elastic limit at all and AQA's own wording conflates the two, so this is recorded rather than corrected.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3 uses only 'limit of proportionality' and 'inelastically deformed'; the phrase 'elastic limit' does not appear

summary: Eight lessons checked against AQA GCSE Physics 8463; 22 findings (3 HIGH, 12 MEDIUM, 7 LOW; 17 FIX, 1 ADJUDICATE, 4 NOTE) and 65 edits. Every worked example recomputes correctly - resultant force 4800 - 1200 = 3600 N and a = 3 m/s2, W = Fs = 200 J, Ee = 0.5ke^2 = 0.45 J and 1.0 J, a = 4 m/s2, v^2 = u^2 + 2as giving 40 m, reaction time 0.6 s, a 9 m/s collision, a 52.1 m braking distance, v = f lambda giving 330 m/s and 300 m/s, a 1.5 m radio wavelength and F = BIl = 0.3 N - so the yield is not arithmetic but the same two build faults as the Combined Science sibling this unit was cut from. First, tier: the higher-only wrapper is on the wrong sections, hiding elastic potential energy and elastic deformation in lesson 2 and v^2 = u^2 + 2as in lesson 3 from Foundation students, while genuinely Higher-tier material (momentum and vehicle safety, the motor effect, F = BIl, Fleming's rule, free body diagrams, inertia, the area under a velocity-time graph, tangents, circular motion) is tested untiered in about forty questions, checks and flashcards, now prefixed, and the motor-effect wrapper is moved up to cover the definition. Second, scope: this 8-lesson unit was cut from a 13-lesson Combined sequence, so it omits most separate-Physics-only Paper 2 content - moments and gears, pressure in fluids, sound and ultrasound, lenses and colour, black bodies, induction and transformers, and the whole of Space physics - which is the unit-level ADJUDICATE. Outright errors: g given as 10 N/kg where AQA uses 9.8, permanent magnets said to be made from iron, the ripple-tank required practical described as a reflection and diffraction investigation, required practical 7 described with only half its method, required practical 9 on light missing entirely, diffraction taught as examinable when the word appears nowhere in the spec, and ABS listed among safety features that work by extending collision time.
